source: He may not look like a man of the cloth, but I assure you his stature is legitimate.
Aye, my lord.
None from me!
Or me. Or anyone, if they know what's good for 'em!
My whole heart, for my whole life. This, I promise you.
...And I you.
(...Of course, knowing everything I know about Claudius—what he's done—what's been done to him—)
(Is this right? Is this something I could ever want?)
(Or is this merely an exploration of all possible worlds? An attempt to sate some sick curiosity?)
(I cannot know for certain.)
(Even knowing everything I know about Claudius... I stand here, again.)
(The Book of Fates will make this reality, if I really want it...)
My lord, I beg you now to turn your attention to the war front. We've received news that Norwegian soldiers are on their way.
If we act now, we can secure the castle and repel them.
Yes, to arms, to arms! Barricade the gates. We've not a moment to spare or a life to lose.
After all, there's to be a wedding in several weeks' time!
Shall we plan a grand celebration?
(...No. I can already feel myself slipping away.)
(But I could use the Book of Fates to keep this world forever, and to become Queen. Just like Simona before me.)
As my family and friends trickle from the chapel, I feel a familiar yanking sensation...

source: (No, there won't be. At least, not yet.)
(I must first uncover what keeps me here.)
My King, where is Prince Hamlet?
I witnessed his ship's return, but haven't heard or seen him anywhere.
...Now, I suppose, is a timely moment. Everyone, I have somber news.
Is... it about Hamlet?
The Prince is dead.
He met his end at sea. I've been informed by the remaining crew.
He went mad once he could no longer see land. He slew the ship's captain, as well as his dearest friends, Ladies Rosencrantz and Guildenstern.
It is only by the good Lord's grace that he was subdued by the remaining crew.
N...no... is it... can it be true? It can't, can it...?
We should mourn Hamlet, and mourn what he became, but know his soul sleeps peacefully now in God's tender arms.
T-this... no...
A life for a life. Ophelia, our father's death is revenged.
Ophelia... how did it happen? How did he... die?
Apologies, my lady. It... all happened so quickly, I cannot recall the details.
He was broken, but he didn't deserve to die.
Hamlet, Hamlet...
Is it really true you didn't witness Hamlet's death?
I see. You don't have to say anything.
But, thank you. Thank you for father. For me. You did what was right.
The King has requested your presence in his private chambers.
I am to indicate that this... is not a request you can deny.
I wonder what he wants. Perhaps I've said something amiss.
He's going to kill me, Bernardo.
Please don't take me there.
I would never let that happen, Ophelia.
Besides, I cannot refuse the King's request either. I am at his command, too.
If anything odd happens, we'll leave. You have my word.
Wonderful. You've come.
Firstly: Thank you for coming right to me to dispel such an insidious rumor.
Firstly: Thank you for bringing to my attention such an insidious rumor.
I would naturally have preferred you come to me instead of troubling my wife, but it can't be helped.
I hear you have recently learned of an insidious rumor. It was good of you to investigate it.
I would have preferred you come to me instead of spreading the lie, but it can't be helped.
Your behavior befits a woman of your standing. And it is appreciated.
Now leave us, Bernardo.
My lord, I don't think that's wise.
Did I ask you to speak? No. Go.
I won't. I can't.
Do you want everyone to know the truth about you?
Ophelia already knows who I am. All of me. And she taught me that I've nothing to hide.
So I'll be taking her and leaving, now.
This is treason!
I'm not so certain others would see it that way.
The Lord knows what is in your heart. And Ophelia and I both do, too. If you act against us, we'll tell the others.
Let's go, Ophelia.
He was going to kill me, wasn't he?
He may still very well try.
Please be careful. I'll have my men keep a close watch on your chamber.
You put your life on the line for me. I'll never forget that.
I already know.
I know about you, Katherine. I know, too, that Claudius has been trying to keep you living in fear.
But I want you to know that I stand by you, no matter what.
And what Claudius tells you... that others would hate you... that's a lie.
I promise you.
So please. Don't abandon me to him. He'll kill me. And you know that now, don't you?
I am not certain how you know this.
But Claudius, I'll be taking her and leaving, now.
I am not so certain others would see it that way.
I don't... know how you found out about me. But please... don't tell anyone.
For now, that's a part of me I'm not ready to discuss with others.
Of course. I understand.
I'm sorry, Ophelia.
I'll leave you two alone.
Unfortunately for you, it's no rumor.
It's true. I murdered my brother. I poured poison into his ear as he slept. How you learned it is no concern of mine.
Everyone thinks him a hero. But I know the truth. I know what he really was: a monster, like my father before him. And... like me.
All we beget is monsters, this family. All we know how to do is hurt. An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth.
But now I am the last monster alive.
You need to come clean—tell the rest of the castle.
At the very least, Hamlet and the Queen... they deserve to know, don't they?
You poor idiot girl.
That won't be happening.
It'll be rather a nuisance to have you disposed of. But one I must suffer nonetheless.
Now die.
A pawn in someone's larger schemes.

source: Ophelia was telling me of a strange nightmare she had. It reminded me to ask you of your own dreams.
Biene... it's clear something has been weighing heavily on you. You've visited me more and more as of late.
I... I need to hide away, just for a bit. Do you mind if I just stay a while as you clean up?
Of course not. I'm always glad to see you.
Though I must ask, Biene, why you do not go to your husband in times like these?
Well, there's... something I wanted to speak to you about. I couldn't tell him.
It's about Hamlet. My husband, I mean. Well—former—husband, that is.
Irma, do you... believe in the power that dreams hold?
Aye, my lady. I believe the Lord sends us visions through dreams, to inspire us to follow His word in our waking hours.
Are you ever... afraid of them?
Sometimes. But I believe we grow stronger through the Lord in confronting them. Why do you ask?
Ophelia said something to me about a nightmare she had, and...
I keep having this... dream. That my husband Hamlet is trapped somewhere, calling to me...
As though he's somewhere underneath me, under the floor. And I run through the castle, trying to find him, but his voice keeps echoing from below...
T-then I realize, I need to go under the floor. As long as I'm running above him, I can't reach him. And he's in pain. He's screaming now.
Crying, begging me to help him.
So I... start to dig... with my fingernails on the stone...
No, you must listen—
A-and my fingers are bleeding, the nails torn right off, but I c-can't stop myself—I have to help him—
Then I finally reach the layer of dirt under the cobblestones, and I pull the first stone away from the earth.
And I see his face. He's dead. I see the deathly white skin, shrunken and stretched horribly over his skull, like a grimace—
My lady! Stop—
No! Irma, I can't stop seeing him! Every time I close my eyes—
I loved him so much, so damned much, I just—
Why did he have to die and not take me with him, Irma?
Why didn't God kill me, too?
Why must I live through this hell? Why can't I go with him?
I t-think the dream is his way of telling me...
That he's unhappy, and suffering, even in death...
Oh, Gerta...
Come here. Let me dry your eyes, love.
I loved him, Irma.
And I love Claudius. I do. But not like him. It's not the same.
It all happened so quickly, Biene. The death, the funeral, and the wedding. It was over so soon.
I just wish... I could have known... if he wanted me to be happy. If only there was that...
Gerta, we can never know for certain. But you knew his heart.
I can't...
Shh. There, there.
It will pass. The grief will pass. I have lost half a dozen loves in my lifetime, and this I know for certain. But you must give it time.
I... I think I can go now.
Of course, Biene. After all, you have a kingdom to run.
My strong, brave, beautiful girl.
My thanks, Irma.
(Where is it? It must be here.)
(Perhaps inside his desk?)
(No, it isn't here either...)
I'm certain he took it.
But why?
I wonder what she's looking for.
I hope she finds that amulet.
Quince, is it? Well met. I've heard a lot about your work.
And I about yours, my good man! Hee hee...
Although I've already made an arrest, I still felt it important to speak to you.
I'm certain you're wondering about why you were summoned here.
Oh, not at all, not at all. My people find it quite ordinary to be under suspicion, in fact.
Perhaps you even think me to be one of those spies the King is so concerned about.
What brings you down here this morning?
Ophelia told me I ought to speak to you! You see, I'm aware you have a certain enemy within the castle.
A little spy problem, perhaps. You're going to speak to the court about it this morning, aren't you?
How could you—h-how—
Perhaps you are thinking to yourself, even now, that I could be such an enemy.
And if I do? What have you to say?
Then I'd tell you, my good man, that the health of Denmark is foremost in my thoughts.
In fact, I've concocted a lovely plan to out the real spy, if you're so inclined.
A plan, eh?
You see, my performances can rouse certain... strong feelings in all who attend.
Were I to, say, put on a performance that highlighted this spy...
Any cloak-and-dagger type without a heart of steel would quickly turn heel, I think!
I've heard word of your performances having such an effect.
If it becomes necessary, I'll call upon you to do so.
In the meantime, you are free to go. I believe your plea of innocence.
Hmph. What is the meaning of calling me here?
I've a kitchen to run and only these two arms to feed a castle.
